data.narrative:
Quaise Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde that has raised $134M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine peers—one public company (LNZA) and eight private—though the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support median-based valuation. Top private peers include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Given the sparse narrow peer universe, stage-progression analysis is the applicable method. Using total capital raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a typical 2.0x multiplier for Series A to next-stage step-up, the analysis implies a valuation of $268M. This methodology reflects observed patterns in early-stage climate venture but relies on the assumption that raised capital appropriately anchors pre-money value at this stage.

The analysis supports a range of $228M to $308M, centered on $268M, derived from sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier (±15 percent). Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer benchmarks in the narrow stage/sector window, which limits cross-validation of the 2.0x step-up multiplier. A more granular valuation would require either identification of additional same-stage Climate & Energy comparables or bottom-up cash-flow analysis of the company's underlying technology and market opportunity.
